text:
maria: Heads-up — we saw CA keep spinning up small g4dn-style nodegroups in eu-west when batch jobs hit a short peak. It kept bouncing between 2 nodegroups even though we have a bigger gpu-pool available. Anyone seen this pattern before?
liam: hmm. do you have the expander setting? random or price?
maria: --expander=least-waste (we set it last month to try to prefer packing).
anjali: least-waste should prefer filling existing nodegroups. maybe something with scale-down timers or node-template weights?
ioscar: deploy-bot: new deployment graphite/profiler to prod (rev 2026.3.12) :rocket:
maria: ^ that deploy happened right before the spike. Logs show CA decided new nodepool because the binpack calc thought pod fit only on new ng (weird).
kevin: can you paste the CA flags (from cluster-autoscaler manifest)?
maria: sure:
```
--cloud-provider=aws
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-enabled=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--max-node-provision-time=15m
```
liam: two quick guesses: 1) node template priority (weights) on the big gpu pool might be lower, so least-waste prefers smaller ngs; 2) pod topology/taints cause scheduler to see only the smaller ng as compatible.
anjali: also check the nodegroup max/min sizes & surge limits — if big pool was at max, CA will choose another.
maria: big pool min=2 max=50 current=10, small pools are 0-6. in the event it picked a small pool currently at 0.
ioscar: did you set any nodeSelector/affinity on the batch pods?
maria: they have tolerations for gpu, and an affinity: preferGPURegion: eu-west (custom label). Nothing strict.
kevin: CA "least-waste" is sensitive to how it computes leftover resources. If small pool offers exact fractional vCPU/GPU fit it may look better even if larger pool could take them with a tiny waste. Try --expander=binpacking or --expander=most-pods to change behavior.
anjali: also consider --balance-similar-node-groups=false as a test. balance-similar can push CA to spread across node groups to even utilization, which sometimes looks like bouncing.
liam: we ran a sim earlier where adding --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m reduced churn vs 10m. bumping scale-down delay stops CA from immediately preferring small ephemeral pools.
maria: good call. any risk to increasing unneeded time? We want reasonable reclaim but less thrash.
kevin: tradeoff is cost during short spikes; increasing to 15m or 20m is fine for batch if tail latency unaffected.
ioscar: infra-ci: ran a local sim with our workload: toggled expander to binpacking and increase unneeded to 20m -> reduced cross-ng churn by ~78% in 2h sim.
anjali: perfect. Also check --scale-down-delay-after-add (default is 10m?). If CA recently added nodes it may still consider them unremovable; lowering that can help or hurt depending.
liam: CA flag is --scale-down-delay-after-add. We usually set 10m. If your deploy started many pods after node add, CA will avoid removing nodes immediately.
kevin: another angle: nodegroup priority/weighting via provider tags or the cluster-autoscaler node-group priority annotation (like cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority) — ensure big gpu pool has higher priority so CA prefers it when capacity available.
maria: oh we hadn't set that. can we add annotation to ASG/ node instance template?
ioscar: yes for aws-asg you can add tag: k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/node-template/label/<label>=<value> and cluster-autoscaler reads node labels for decisions. Also some setups support node-group priority annotation.
anjali: one more thing: pods that set topologySpreadConstraints or requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution can effectively block placement to big pool if label mismatch. check that.
liam: action list: 1) try expander=binpacking in a canary CA deployment; 2) bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 15-20m; 3) annotate big-gpu nodegroup with higher priority/weight; 4) audit pod affinities/taints; 5) run infra-ci sim after changes.
kevin: +1. I'd also add metrics alert for "scale-churn-rate" (adds+deletes per 10m) so we detect regressions.
maria: planning to test binpacking + 20m unneeded on staging tonight. I'll post results tomorrow AM.
ioscar: have you considered prefix caching (kv) workloads causing weird startup burst? if many pods request warm cache they might temporarily prefer fresh nodes. just a thought.
maria: interesting — profiler deploy had a warm-init job that creates temp GPU pods. Could be.
anjali: if warm jobs are short-lived consider using a dedicated prewarmed pool with min=2 and no autoscaling. That prevents CA from repeatedly adding tiny pools.
liam: FYI if you go that route, mark the prewarm pool with a special label and nodeAffinity so scheduling picks it only for warm jobs.
kevin: ok let's not flip prod flags until staging sim passes. maria, drop the sim logs here after the run. :thumbsup:
maria: will do. thanks all.
infra-ci: simulation summary uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/229001: expander=binpacking + unneeded=20m -> 3x fewer nodegroup creations, small perf impact on startup latency (~1.8s).
kevin: nice. merge plan?
maria: plan: roll to staging 23:00 UTC canary, monitor scale-churn alert for 1h, then prod 03:00 UTC if green.
ioscar: +1. don't forget to include the nodegroup annotation change in the terraform diff.
anjali: and add a quickplaybook note in eng-infra/operations on when to revert if something odd pops.
liam: thanks team.
maria: thanks. will update thread after staging run. :sparkles:
